ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r8.claim: From vv48–77 the text lists celebrated prophets in ascending order, beginning with Moses and Abraham; p92 continues that their message matches the Qur’an's.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p449/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p449/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p449/r1.claim: After proving his case, Ibrahim rebukes them for worshipping statues that can neither benefit nor harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p449/r1.anchor: ولما ظهرت الحجة عليهم أخذ يقرعهم ويوبخهم بعباده تماثيل ما لا ينفع ولا يضر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r3.claim: The rebuke of worshipping what cannot help or harm suggests that needy creatures foolishly seek aid from other needy creatures.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r3.anchor: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r4.speaker: حمدون القصار
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r4.claim: Hamdun compares creatures seeking help from creatures to one prisoner relying on another prisoner.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p108#2/r4.anchor: وقال حمدون القصار : استعانة الخلق بالخلق كاستعانة المسجون بالمسجون

ASAD-NOTES:21:66/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:66/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:66/r1.claim: Abraham argues that idols are unworthy of worship because they can neither benefit nor harm, and urges his people to reason.
ASAD-NOTES:21:66/r1.anchor: Do you then worship, instead of God, something that cannot benefit you in any way, nor harm you?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r6.claim: After 21:24’s reference to the teaching of earlier prophets, the passage names prophets who founded nations: Moses first as the last prior law-bearing messenger, with Aaron as helper; then Abraham and his descendants’ two branches, followed by Noah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r6.anchor: those prophets are mentioned in a sequence who were the founders of their respective nations. Just before Muḥammad (sws), Moses (sws) was the messenger who was bestowed sharī‘ah from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r7.claim: Abraham is presented as founder and leader of the Israelite and Ishmaelite branches, explaining the allusions to Isaac, Jacob, and Lot in this sequence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p120/r7.anchor: Abraham (sws) is mentioned who was the founder of nations and the leader of both branches of his progeny – the Israelites and the Ishmaelites.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p121/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p121/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p121/r1.claim: The prophetic sequence evokes the whole history of guidance: Muhammad's opponents receive the guidance given to earlier peoples, and persistent rejection will bring them the fate of earlier deniers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p129/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p129/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p129/r4.claim: After the people admitted the idols' inability to speak, Abraham's question about worshipping powerless beings landed forcefully because their helplessness was already evident.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p129/r4.anchor: They could only have had the required impact after the helplessness of the idols had become evident.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r1.claim: Abraham rebukes them with a question meaning: knowing the idols' condition, do you still worship them?

ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r2.claim: The idols benefit you not at all; alternatively, the phrase may mean that they do not benefit you in anything.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r2.anchor: ما لا ينفعكم شيئا من النفع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r3.claim: Knowing the idols' state, which is incompatible with divinity, necessarily requires refraining from worshipping them.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p67#2/r3.anchor: فإن العلم بحاله المنافية للألوهية مما يوجب الإجتناب عن عبادته قطعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p326/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p326/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p326/r4.claim: Abraham asks why they worship things that can neither benefit them if worshipped nor harm them if left alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p326/r4.anchor: أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا} إن عبدتموه، {ولا يضركم} إن تركتم عبادته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:64-67/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:64-67/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:64-67/r6.claim: Abraham rebukes worship of things that cannot benefit or harm, contradicting their admission that the idols are inert.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:64-67/r6.anchor: إنكار لعبادتهم لها بعد اعترافهم بأنها جمادات لا تنفع ولا تضر فإنه ينافي الألوهية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r5.claim: Abraham rebukes them for worshipping beneath God, the supreme sovereign who alone controls benefit and harm through His complete attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r5.anchor: منكرا عليهم موبخا لهم مسببا عن إقرارهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r6.claim: Because they urgently seek help after their idols were smashed, Abraham puts benefit first: the idols can neither provide what they hope for nor cause what they fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p94/r6.anchor: بسبب تكسير أصنامهم , راجين من ينفعهم في ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p380/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p380/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p380/r3.claim: Abraham rebukes them for knowingly worshipping something that can neither benefit them if worshipped nor harm them if neglected; such knowledge demands abandoning its worship.
BURSEVI:v5p380/r3.anchor: أتعلمون ذلك فتعبدون {من دون الله} أي : حال كونكم متجاوزين

BURSEVI:v5p380/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p380/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v5p380/r7.claim: Ibn Ata says God calls people to Himself and cuts them off from all else: why rely on an equally helpless creature instead of the One who controls harm, benefit, and the return.
BURSEVI:v5p380/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء دعا الله تعالى عباده إليه وقطعهم عما دونه بقوله : {أفتعبدون}

BURSEVI:v5p380/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p380/r8.speaker: حمدون القصار
BURSEVI:v5p380/r8.claim: Hamdun al-Qassar says that creatures seeking help from creatures is like one prisoner seeking help from another.
BURSEVI:v5p380/r8.anchor: قال حمدون القصار : استغاثة الخلق بالخلق كاستغاثة المسجون بالمسجون

BURSEVI:v5p380/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p380/r9.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p380/r9.claim: Some spiritual masters say seeking another reveals distance from God; all besides Him is play and falsehood, so detach from all else and rely on the Lord, who suffices for every need.
BURSEVI:v5p380/r9.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار طلبك من غيره لوجود بعدك عنه إذ لو كنت حاضرا بقلبك معه

BURSEVI:v5p380/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p380/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p380/r10.claim: Habib al-Ajami's wife urged him to earn wages; after he worshipped all night, he said he had worked for the Generous One and was ashamed to ask payment. Three days later she demanded wages or divorce; the next night he returned to find food and a bag of gold, sent by God, and she repented.
BURSEVI:v5p380/r10.anchor: حكي أن امرأة حبيب العجمي ألحت عليه أن يعمل بالأجرة طلبا للسعة في الرزق فخرج من بيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r5.claim: Abraham turns their admission into a disavowal of idol worship and adds that idols can neither benefit nor harm their worshippers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r5.anchor: فلما اعترفوا بأن الأصنام لا تستطيع النطق انتهز إبراهيم الفرصة لإرشادهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r6.claim: Inability to speak entails inability to benefit or harm: without speech to communicate, idols lack mind and its capacities of knowledge, will, and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p104/r6.anchor: وجعل عدم استطاعتها النفع والضر ملزوما لعدم النطق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.claim: Abraham rebukes them for worshipping images that have no power to benefit or harm in themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.anchor: ووقفهم موبخا على عبادتهم تماثيل لا تنفع بذاتها ولا تضر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p365/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p365/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p365/r1.claim: Abraham rebukes them for worshipping idols that neither provide or give them anything nor harm them if left unworshipped, urging them to worship the One who owns benefit and harm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p365/r1.anchor: فحينئذ توجهت لإبراهيم الحجة فقال موبخا لهم أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم أي لا يرزقكم ولا يعطيكم شيئا ولا يضركم إذا لم تعبدوه وفي هذا حث لهم على عبادة من يملك النفع والضر

MUQATIL:21:66-70/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:66-70/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:66-70/r1.claim: Ibrahim asks why they worship idols that cannot benefit them if worshipped or harm them if left unworshipped.
MUQATIL:21:66-70/r1.anchor: إن عبدتموهم { ولا يضركم } [آية: 66] إن لم تعبدوهم.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r1.claim: Abraham speaks here to make an argument against his people.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r2.claim: “Anything” is a verbal noun meaning “benefit”; the idols neither benefit nor harm those who do not worship them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p85#3/r2.anchor: ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ﴾ هو في موضع المصدر أي نفعا ﴿ ولا يضركم ﴾ أن لم تعبدوه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:64-67/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:64-67/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:64-67/r4.claim: Abraham cuts off their argument by asking why they worship what can neither benefit nor harm them; أف means “filth” or “stinking” for them and their idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:64-67/r4.anchor: أي النتن لكم { ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون }

QASHANI:21:66-67/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:66-67/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:66-67/r1.claim: Worship and reverence belong to God alone: nothing else benefits or harms, since He is the sole beneficial and harmful agent.
QASHANI:21:66-67/r1.anchor: وتعظمون غيره مما لا ينفع ولا يضر، إذ هو النافع الضار لا غير

RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains af as a sound whose utterance signals that the speaker is annoyed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أف صوت إذا صوت به علم أن صاحبه متضجر

RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r3.claim: Abraham was exasperated by their persistence in worship after their excuse failed and truth became clear, so he voiced his displeasure.
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r3.anchor: وإن إبراهيم عليه السلام أضجره ما رأى من ثباتهم على عبادتها بعد انقطاع عذرهم ، وبعد وضوح الحق وزهوق الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r4.claim: One possibility is that Abraham spoke after they had already recognized that his argument was sound.
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r4.anchor: ثم يحتمل أنه قال لهم ذلك وقد عرفوا صحة قوله

RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r5.claim: Another possibility is that the proof had become apparent although they had not understood it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أنه قال لهم ذلك وقد ظهرت الحجة وإن لم يعقلوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p161#2/r6.claim: Razi favors the second timing: the proof was evident but they had not grasped it, as suggested by Abraham's questions about worship and reasoning.

STUDYQURAN:21:66/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:66/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:66/r1.claim: The Quran makes similar points and asks similar questions about idols’ inability to help or harm in the listed verses.
STUDYQURAN:21:66/r1.anchor: Similar statements and questions regarding the inability of idols to help or harm can be found in 5:76; 6:71; 10:18, 106; 13:16; 20:89; 22:12; 25:55.

SULAMI:v2p8#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r1.claim: God calls servants to Him and cuts them off from all besides Him: why rely on a powerless being like oneself instead of the One who controls harm, benefit, and the return?
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : دعا الله عز وجل عباده إليه ، وقطعهم عما دونه

SULAMI:v2p8#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r2.speaker: حمدون القصار
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r2.claim: One creature’s appeal for help to another is like a prisoner appealing to another prisoner.
SULAMI:v2p8#3/r2.anchor: قال حمدون القصار : استغاثة الخلق بالخلق كاستغاثة المسجون بالمسجون

TABATABAI:21:65-69/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r3.claim: Abraham does not defend himself; he turns their admission that idols cannot speak into a proof that they know and can do nothing, can neither benefit nor harm, and therefore are unworthy of worship.
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r3.anchor: لازم كونهم لا ينطقون أن لا يعلموا شيئا ولا يقدروا على شيء، ولازم ذلك أن لا ينفعوكم شيئا

TABATABAI:21:65-69/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r4.claim: Worship is pointless when its objects can neither benefit nor harm, since worship is undertaken either in hope of good or in fear of harm.
TABATABAI:21:65-69/r4.anchor: أن يكون عبادتهم لغوا إذ العبادة إما لرجاء خير أو لخوف شر وليس عندهم شيء من ذلك

TABRISI:21:64-68/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:64-68/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:64-68/r9.claim: Abraham rebukes worship of idols that neither benefit nor harm; if they could do either, they would have defended themselves.
TABRISI:21:64-68/r9.anchor: أي أفتوجهون عبادتكم إلى الأصنام التي لا تنفعكم شيئا إن عبدتموها ولا تضركم إن تركتموها

TABRISI:21:64-68/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:64-68/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:64-68/r10.claim: Power to harm or benefit alone is insufficient for worship; only the creator of life, desire, power, and reason, who can reward and punish, deserves worship.
TABRISI:21:64-68/r10.anchor: ليس كل من قدر على الضر والنفع استحق العبادة وإنما يستحقها من قدر على أصول النعم التي هي الحياة والشهوة والقدرة وكمال العقل

THALABI:v6p280/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p280/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p280/r12.claim: Ibrahim argues that idols are unworthy of worship because they can neither benefit nor harm their worshippers; the rebuke follows from their admitted incapacity.
THALABI:v6p280/r12.anchor: أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r1.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says idols neither provide nor give anything, and if people do not worship them they cause no harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r1.anchor: قال السدي: يقول لا يرزقكم ولا يعطيكم شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says idols do no good when worshiped and no harm when abandoned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكلبي: لا ينفعكم إن عبدتموه ولا يضركم إن تركتموه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r3.claim: After the admission made the proof decisive, Abraham rebukes them; the argument urges worship of God, who controls benefit through reward for worship and harm through punishment for failing to worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p119/r3.anchor: فلما اتجهت الحجة عليهم بإقرارهم وبخهم إبراهيم فقال

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p323/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p323/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p323/r3.claim: The powerless things worshipped besides God are their idols.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r1.claim: The idolaters’ admission that their gods could not speak exposed their incapacity and gave Abraham a chance to show how absurd their faith was.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r1.anchor: Putperestlerin İbrâhim’e, “Sen bunların konuşmadığını pekâlâ biliyorsun” demeleri, açıkça kendilerinin de tanrılarının âcizliğini itiraf etmelerinden başka bir şey değildi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r2.claim: Because of their bigotry, the idolaters could not endure Abraham’s criticism and decided to burn him, protecting their gods instead of expecting their gods to protect them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:66/r2.anchor: taassupları sebebiyle bu eleştiriye tahammül edemeyen putperestler İbrâhim’i yakmaya karar verdiler ve böylece tanrılarının onları koruması gerekirken, onlar tanrılarını korumak istediler

BURHAN:v1p120/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r5.claim: Harm usually precedes benefit because worshippers first fear punishment, then hope for reward; benefit comes first where the benefit is foregrounded.
BURHAN:v1p120/r5.anchor: ومنه تقديم لفظ الضرر على النفع فى الأكثر لأن العابد يعبد معبودا خوفا من عقابه أولا ثم طمعا فى ثوابه

BURHAN:v1p120/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r6.claim: Benefit precedes harm in seven places: three use nouns and four verbs; in al-Aʿraf the sequence follows prior references to guidance and good before evil.
BURHAN:v1p120/r6.anchor: وحيث تقدم النفع على الضر فلتقدم ما يتضمن النفع

BURHAN:v1p122/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p122/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p122/r6.claim: In the story of Abraham, the idols' inability to speak in the preceding exchange leads into the question why they are worshipped when they can neither benefit nor harm.
BURHAN:v1p122/r6.anchor: وفى الأنبياء تقدم قول الكفار لإبراهيم فى المجادلة

BURHAN:v1p122/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p122/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p122/r8.claim: Across these examples, the order varies with each passage's context, creating consistent coherence rather than mechanical repetition.
BURHAN:v1p122/r8.anchor: فتأمل هذه المواضع المطردة التى هى أعظم اتساقا من العقود

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r3.claim: At 21:66, the verse's ending also differs from the sura's usual rhyme, underscoring that the intended meaning governs the wording.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r3.anchor: في سورة الأنبياء الآية (قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ {66} ) مغايرة لباقي آيات السورة
